frames.label: In aluminum machining, a common practice is to use an oil–water emulsion coolant (“mouse milk”) delivered by a pump-d...
frames.main_point: In aluminum machining, a common practice is to use an oil–water emulsion coolant (“mouse milk”) delivered by a pump-directed nozzle at the cut, with a sump that collects and recirculates the fluid back to the nozzle.
frames.source_quote: Note also that aluminum machining processes commonly use an oil-and-water emulsion called "mouse milk" as a lubricant, with a pump-driven feed nozzle aimed right at the hole, and a sump system that catches the used fluid and recycles it through a storage vessel and back to the nozzle again.
frames.subject: oil-and-water emulsion coolant (“mouse milk”) with recirculating sump for aluminum machining

frames.main_point: CNC machine coolant in the sump tends to run richer than the target concentration, so makeup additions should be mixed lean (around 2–3%) to bring the overall concentration back toward the setpoint.
frames.source_quote: Present concentration in the machine sump will almost always be richer than required, so I need to 'dose' the makeup liquid at a concentration of 2-3% to balance the concentration in the sump.
